question: Can the janitor-fish evidence reported at Paitan Lake be traced to an accessible taxonomic report or independently verifiable specimen record, and does the conflicting 2009 report establish presence or absence?
decision: Retain a historical Paitan janitor-fish locality lead only. The 2005 and 2006 news reports attribute identification to Edna Agasen and Jonathan Armbruster, but the original unpublished report and specimens were not accessed. The 2005 story prints Pterygoplichthys parotalis, while the 2006 story prints P. pardalis. Later official and technical summaries repeat Paitan as a genus-level Pterygoplichthys locality or cite the same inaccessible report; they are not independent specimen confirmations. Punto's 2009 article reports both an alleged DENR check finding none and a DENR-attributed P. pardalis statement without dates or methods. The conflict remains indeterminate; no current presence or absence claim is supported.

sourceTrace.title: Janitor fish, anyone?
sourceTrace.sourceType: news article relaying a PCAMRD statement
sourceTrace.finding: Attributes identification to Edna Agasen with assistance from Jonathan Armbruster and prints Pterygoplichthys parotalis for Marikina River and Lake Paitan, Cuyapo.
sourceTrace.limits: No collection date, method, specimen identifier, voucher, or underlying report is provided.
sourceTrace.disposition: Historical secondary locality lead; preserve the printed spelling and do not silently correct it or treat the story as specimen-level verification.

sourceTrace.finding: Attributes identification to Agasen and Armbruster and prints Pterygoplichthys pardalis for Marikina River and Lake Paitan. It separately reports a photo-based P. disjunctivus identification from Agusan Marsh, outside this Paitan review.
sourceTrace.lineage: Repeats the same named experts and locality claim as the 2005 Philstar item, with a changed species spelling. Treat the articles as one related claim chain, not independent detections.
sourceTrace.disposition: Historical secondary locality lead only; no Paitan specimen chain is supplied.

sourceTrace.title: New Philippine record of South American sailfin catfishes (Pisces: Loricariidae)
sourceTrace.sourceType: peer-reviewed taxonomic study with examined specimens
sourceTrace.finding: Reports 193 examined specimens and identifies Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus and P. pardalis. Its five named collection sites are Marikina River, Pasig River, Catmon Creek, Banilad Creek, and Laguna de Bay at San Pedro. Paitan Lake is not among them.
sourceTrace.disposition: Taxonomic and nearby-basin comparator only; neither verifies nor disproves the separate Paitan lead.

sourceTrace.title: Ecological Risk Screening Summary: Amazon Sailfin Catfish (Pterygoplichthys pardalis)
sourceTrace.finding: Repeats the Paitan locality under Agasen 2005 and explicitly lists the Agasen report among references quoted but not accessed.
sourceTrace.disposition: Claim-lineage evidence only; not an independent Paitan record.

sourceTrace.title: P.S. Resolution No. 1020, Fourteenth Congress, Second Regular Session
sourceTrace.finding: Says recent reports place janitor fish in Lake Paitan and attributes a P. pardalis/Paitan statement to DENR. The resolution directs an inquiry and gives no survey protocol, specimen, collection date, or accession.
sourceTrace.disposition: Official record of statements and concerns, not an independent biological survey.

sourceTrace.title: Ecija execs deny presence of janitor fish in huge lake
sourceTrace.sourceType: news report quoting local officials and a DENR-attributed statement
sourceTrace.finding: The mayor says a DENR team checked a report and found none; later, the same article attributes a P. pardalis/Paitan statement to DENR.
sourceTrace.limits: No dates, station, effort, method, identification record, or specimen accompany the alleged check. The statements could refer to different times or information chains.
sourceTrace.disposition: Indeterminate historical conflict lead; neither statement establishes current status.

sourceTrace.title: National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan (NISSAP) 2020–2030
sourceTrace.sourceType: official national strategy and secondary synthesis
sourceTrace.finding: Box 2.3 names Pterygoplichthys spp. and lists Lake Paitan among reported invasive locations, while discussing P. disjunctivus and P. pardalis as genus-level context. Its grouped citations do not provide a Paitan-specific specimen table.
sourceTrace.disposition: Official synthesis supports a historical genus-level report trail, not species-specific or current presence.

sourceNameStrings.status: unresolved source spelling; no correction made

sourceNameStrings.taxonomyCheck: Pterygoplichthys pardalis is a valid name in the Catalog of Fishes / ITIS cross-reference. This nomenclatural result does not verify that the Paitan fish was this species.
sourceNameStrings.status: valid taxon name; Paitan identification not independently specimen-verified
genus-level synthesis; do not split into P. pardalis and P. disjunctivus at Paitan

taxonomicReview.decision: Do not silently normalize the 2005 spelling difference or convert the shared vernacular label janitor fish into a species identification.

relatedClaimChains: The 2005 and 2006 Philstar articles cite the same Agasen/Armbruster identification narrative; the original Agasen report was not accessed.
The USFWS risk screen repeats Agasen 2005 and says that reference was quoted but not accessed.
The Senate resolution and 2009 Punto article relay DENR-attributed statements without an independent specimen record.
NISSAP gives a broad Pterygoplichthys genus-level synthesis with grouped secondary citations.
Chavez et al. (2006) is an independent taxonomic specimen study in the Laguna de Bay basin, but its five named sites exclude Paitan.
independenceAssessment.fishbaseReferenceAnomaly: FishBase's Philippines species page repeats the Paitan locality and cites Agasen reference 53891; its bibliography page lists the report year as 2050. The USFWS reference list gives 2005 while noting the original was not accessed. Neither resolves the year or provides the report.

rightsAndUse.reviewedMaterials: Publisher news pages, official Senate and PhilCHM PDFs, the publisher-hosted Zootaxa article, FishBase reference metadata, and the USFWS risk-screen PDF were reviewed for concise source-reported facts and provenance.
rightsAndUse.decision: Retain concise attributed findings and source lineage for internal research triage only; no figures, photographs, tables, or extended text reproduced.

nextStep: Seek the original Agasen 2005 unpublished report or a specimen/accession trail that names Paitan, dates the collection, and supports species-level diagnosis. If the report cannot be retrieved, search independently catalogued dated Paitan specimens or a site-level survey; keep this lead and the 2009 conflict research-only. Continue separate Vaca Dam Reservoir inventory work and leave Central Luzon incomplete.
